intro: Armenia's political landscape is dominated by the publication of a new draft constitution and the formal launch of the TRIPP transport corridor project, while diplomatic engagements with the EU and the US continue.

topics.title: New draft constitution published and debated
topics.text: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has published a draft of a new constitution that proposes significant changes, including the removal of references to the Declaration of Independence and Mount Ararat from state symbols, granting the Prime Minister the role of army supreme commander in peacetime, and allowing courts to strip citizenship in certain cases. Opposition forces and the ARF have criticized the draft as democratic backsliding and rejected a referendum deal, while Baku has stated it highly appreciates the document. Civil society discussions and expert analyses are ongoing regarding the specific legal implications.

topics.title: TRIPP transport corridor project launches practical phase
topics.text: Prime Minister Pashinyan and former US President Donald Trump announced the start of practical work on the TRIPP (Trans-Armenia Railway) project, described as the largest economic project since independence. Construction has begun on the 'Trump Route' in Meghri, and Iran intends to closely monitor implementation. Pashinyan discussed the project with EU ambassadors, while Azerbaijan's President Aliyev thanked Trump for the launch.

topics.title: Pashinyan invited to Washington for National Prayer Breakfast and Trump meeting
topics.text: Former US President Donald Trump has invited Prime Minister Pashinyan to Washington for a meeting and the National Prayer Breakfast. The invitation was conveyed by a special envoy's senior advisor and confirmed by the Armenian Prime Minister's office and the Foreign Ministry.

topics.title: EU-Armenia relations advance with visa liberalization talks
topics.text: Prime Minister Pashinyan met with ambassadors of EU member states and the Speaker of Parliament met with heads of EU diplomatic missions to discuss deepening relations, visa liberalization, and the TRIPP project. The Armenian Foreign Minister also reaffirmed Italy's full support for the peace process with Azerbaijan during separate talks.

topics.title: Armenia recalls six ambassadors and NATO mission head
topics.text: The Armenian government has recalled six ambassadors and the head of the mission to NATO, signaling a significant reshuffle in the country's diplomatic corps.

topics.title: Economic activity grows 6.9% in first nine months; DigiTec 2026 highlights AI sector
topics.text: The World Bank reported that Armenia's economic activity rose 6.9% in the first nine months of the year. The DigiTec 2026 expo in Yerevan closed after bringing global AI conversations to Armenia, with Ardshinbank presenting a new approach to banking and AUA launching a Physical AI program.

topics.title: Diaspora communities mark cultural and advocacy milestones
topics.text: San Diego's St. Sarkis Church raised $200,000 for a new community hall at its 'Gala Esperanza'. The ANCA Eastern Region will honor US Senators Reed and Whitehouse with the Freedom Award, while ANC International welcomed the ICJ ruling on the Rohingya genocide as a step toward justice for all victims. The California Courier published an opinion piece calling for Pashinyan to face life in prison.
